title: Close a 300 mm wafer shipping box in the maker's order: left edge in and latched, right side pressed flush and latched
instruction: Close the wafer shipping box. Carry its door by the two D-ring handles, set its left edge into the opening first and latch that side, then press the right side flush and latch it. Fold both D-rings down and let go.
context: 300 mm wafers, the substrate of every AI chip, travel from the wafer maker to the fab in front-opening shipping boxes (FOSBs), and fab and R&D staff re-pack them by hand (no count of how often is published). The box maker's manual for the SB300 gives the door's manual assembly: 'Grip the door and shipper box along the vertical edge (pivot edge) with one hand and rotate the door until the wafer cushion contacts the wafers. Latch the lock on the pivot edge first... Apply inward pressure to the opposite side of the door until it is flush to the shipper box opening and latch closed', and 'Make sure the door is properly seated before engaging the latches.' The cushion presses on 25 wafers, so the far side springs back out until it is held flush. While the first latch is turned the door is held only at its pivot edge, so the other hand must hold it. Tested: a set order, then a press held against a spring while the other hand latches.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench top. (1) A 300 mm wafer shipping box in the size of the Entegris SB300 (385 wide, 333 deep, 337 tall, published), clear polycarbonate, about 7 kg (estimate), standing on a 2 cm printed plate (the maker's three-pin kinematic coupling is not modelled: the box is held by friction, 1.2). Its opening faces the robot: the rim's front face is at x = 34, centred at y = 0. The opening is 34 wide and 25 tall, centred 20.4 cm above the bench; the rim is 1.2 cm deep. It holds 25 wafers, 300 mm across and 0.775 mm thick, 10 mm apart, the first 44 mm above the box's floor (published pitch), their front edges 1.8 cm behind the rim's face. The wafers are fixed in the box's shape. (2) The door: clear polycarbonate, 363.7 wide and 258.0 tall (published), 2.5 cm thick and 1.0 kg (estimates). It stands on a printed rest (a 7.5 cm tall block with two 3.5 cm rails 2.8 cm apart) with its inner face at x = 28 and its centre 20.4 cm above the bench, centred at y = 0. On its inner face two spring pads, 2 x 2.5 cm, at y = +4.5 and -4.5, stand 3.3 cm proud and stand for the wafer cushion: each is a spring of 875 N/m, 14 N together at flush (estimate; the manual gives no force). (3) Two D-rings on the door's outer face at y = +15 and -15, mid-height: a 12 mm square bar, 5.2 cm long, on two 10 mm legs 4 cm apart, standing 3.6 cm proud of the face when lifted. They start lifted, with the bar upright. Each ring turns about its stem (a quarter turn, 90 degrees counter-clockwise seen from the robot latches it; the cam is set at 1 N m, an assumption within the manual's 4.4 N m maximum) and, after that, folds down onto the door. A latch counts as engaged only when its ring is turned 80 degrees or more while its side of the door is within 1 mm of flush on the box; an engaged latch holds its side to the rim with 12 N. Nothing else is on the bench. Run limit 3,000 steps (20 Hz). Real trial: a used SB300 or any 300 mm FOSB with 25 reclaim wafers (any 775 um wafer: only the cushion's push matters), the printed plate and rest, and a pencil outline of the box on the plate. Reset: unlatch both rings, lift them, set the door back on its rest. Entegris and SB300 are trademarks of Entegris, Inc., named for identification only.
scoring: 0 if the box moves more than 5 mm on its plate (read against the pencil outline) or lifts off the plate for half a second, the door drops, the door meets the wafers more than 5 degrees out of square, or the right latch engages before the left. 0.25: the left latch engaged (the left edge within 1 mm of flush). 0.5: both latched. 0.75: also the door flush all round (a 0.5 mm feeler does not enter at any of the four corners). 1.0: also both D-rings folded flat (80 degrees or more), both pads pressed 6 mm or more (the cushion on the wafers), both grippers 3 cm clear, still for 1 s. Real trial: feeler at the corners, the latch order from the video, the cushion on the wafers seen through the clear door. The pad-pressed and 5-degree checks are simulator readings; a real trial uses the feeler, the latch order on video and a pencil outline.
reset_notes: Both D-rings unlatched and lifted, the door on its rest at x = 28, the box on its plate. No seed changes the scene; the jitter run shifts free parts by up to 1 cm.
fidelity: PhysX at 240 Hz on GPU, rigid parts and sprung joints. The wafers are fixed in the box. The cushion is two spring pads; its 14 N, the 1 kg door and the 1 N m cam torque are estimates, not measured. A latch is a rule: it engages when its ring is turned while its side is flush (1 mm), then holds that side with 12 N; the robot's contact turns the ring and presses the door. The demo reads the door's pose; a policy sees cameras. Meshes are hand-built from published sizes, not vendor CAD.
scores: demo: 1.0 on 3 of 3 README runs (560 of 3,000 steps), 4 of 4 jittered runs and one run on an RTX 5090; Dream-1 run: 0.0 (3,000 steps)
